title: THE WOMAN WHO CAME AFTER THE BABYSITTER LEFT — AND THE SECRET MY HUSBAND HAD BEEN HIDING FOR THREE MONTHS
excerpt: A family mystery • Suspense • Betrayal • An unforgettable twist
author: admin

blocks.text: A family mystery • Suspense • Betrayal • An unforgettable twist

My four-year-old daughter drew a picture of a woman with no face. Just a blank circle where the eyes, nose, and mouth should have been. At first, I thought it was just another one of her strange little drawings.
She was four. Her imagination was enormous, and sometimes the things she drew made absolutely no sense.
But then I asked her a question that would change everything I thought I knew about my family.
“Sweetheart, who’s this?” She looked up from her crayons.
“The lady who watches me when you go to work.” I smiled. “That’s Miss Janet, isn’t it?”

Miss Janet was our babysitter. She had been taking care of my daughter, Lily, for almost a year. She was responsible, kind, and punctual. I paid her fifteen dollars an hour, and she always left before I got home.
But Lily shook her head. “No, Mommy. The other lady.” I stopped smiling. “What other lady?”
“The one who comes after Miss Janet leaves.” My stomach tightened.
I leaned closer. “What lady, sweetheart?” Lily pointed at the faceless woman.
“She comes in the house with her own key. She sits with me in the living room. Sometimes she watches me sleep.” I felt something cold move through my chest. “Does Miss Janet know her?”
Lily shook her head. “Miss Janet says I shouldn’t open the door for strangers. But that lady isn’t a stranger. Daddy knows her.”
For a moment, I couldn’t speak. My husband?

Lily shrugged. “He told me she’s our secret friend.” I stared at my daughter. Then I looked down at the drawing again. The woman had long black hair, a red dress, and something strange drawn around her neck.
A little silver necklace. I didn’t recognize it.
But I would soon learn that the necklace was the smallest part of a secret that had been buried inside my marriage.
And it had been happening right under my roof.
My name is Sarah Mitchell. I’m thirty-four years old, and at the time this happened, I had been married to my husband, Daniel, for seven years.
We had a beautiful four-year-old daughter named Lily.
We lived in a two-story house in a quiet neighborhood outside Columbus, Ohio. Daniel worked in commercial real estate, while I managed operations for a medical supply company.
Our lives weren’t perfect, but I believed we were happy.
Daniel was the kind of husband who remembered birthdays, brought home flowers occasionally, and kissed me before leaving for work.
He was also the person I trusted most in the world.
After Lily was born, we hired Janet, a fifty-eight-year-old retired elementary school teacher, to look after her while we worked.
She knew Lily’s favorite stories, made her little lunches, and never complained when Lily wanted to wear mismatched socks.
She arrived at 8:00 every morning and left at 5:30 in the evening.
That evening, after Lily went to bed, I took the picture to the kitchen and placed it on the counter.
I stared at it for nearly twenty minutes.
Then I opened the Nest doorbell application on my phone.
Maybe Lily had simply dreamed up an imaginary friend.
Janet walked out of the front door carrying her handbag. She locked the door behind her and walked toward her car.
She looked directly at the doorbell camera.
Then she reached into her handbag, pulled out a key, and unlocked my front door.
She didn’t even look around to see whether anyone was watching.
She simply walked inside as if she owned the house.
That was how long this stranger spent inside my house.
Twenty-seven minutes alone with my daughter.
“Janet, I need to ask you something. Have you noticed anyone coming to the house after you leave?”
“Because your husband told me everything was arranged.”
“He said she was a family friend and that she had permission to visit Lily. He told me not to worry.”
“No. She always came after I left. I only saw her a few times when I was putting things in my car.”
“Janet, did Lily ever seem frightened of her?”
“Not exactly. But there was something strange.”
“Your daughter used to ask me why the lady never showed her face in photographs.”
“She told me the woman always turned away whenever Lily tried to take a picture.”
“Janet, did you ever tell Daniel about this?”
“Yes. I mentioned it once. He told me not to make a big deal out of it.”
Then I did something I never imagined I would do.
The officer who arrived was named Detective Robert Hayes.
He was in his early forties, with tired eyes and a calm voice.
He watched the woman enter my house several times without saying anything.
“Does anyone besides you and your husband have a key?”
“Janet has one. My mother has an emergency key. That’s all.”
“Could your husband have given someone another key?”
He asked me for the vehicle registration details visible in the recording.
“Mrs. Mitchell, this vehicle is registered to your husband’s mother.”
Patricia lived nearly forty minutes away.
She visited occasionally, but she had never mentioned coming to our house every afternoon.
